title: Repentance Unto Life
speaker: Mr. Nick Newton

outline.title: Defining Repentance Unto Life
subpoints: Distinguishing godly sorrow from the sorrow of the world
A four-step process: change of mind, regret, lament, and turning again
True repentance results in heart and life change

outline.title: The Antithesis: Repentance Unto Death
subpoints: Examining the case of Judas Iscariot
Undirected remorse leads to death rather than salvation
The necessity of directing sorrow toward the Savior

outline.title: Repentance as an Evangelical Grace
subpoints: Repentance is a gift from God, not a natural human ability
It is integral to the plan of salvation and the gospel
Described as 'saving grace' in the Larger Catechism

outline.title: The Universal Scope of Repentance
subpoints: The gift of repentance is extended to Jews and Gentiles alike
The conversion of Cornelius demonstrates this inclusion
God grants repentance unto life to all the elect under the New Covenant

outline.title: The Necessity of Preaching Repentance
subpoints: Ministers are commanded to preach repentance alongside faith
The doctrine of repentance is inseparable from the gospel message
Preaching repentance is a primary objective of the apostolic mission

summary:
This lesson explores the doctrine of repentance unto life as presented in Chapter 15 of the Westminster Confession of Faith. The speaker defines true repentance as a four-step process involving a change of mind and purpose, internal regret, external lament, and a decisive turn toward God. This godly sorrow is contrasted with the 'sorrow of the world,' which leads to death, illustrated by the tragic example of Judas Iscariot. The distinction highlights that remorse must be directed toward the Savior to result in salvation.

The sermon further examines repentance as an 'evangelical grace,' emphasizing that it is a gift from God rather than a natural human capacity. This grace is integral to the gospel and is described in the Larger Catechism as 'saving grace' because its outcome is eternal life. The speaker notes that this gift is not limited to a specific ethnic group but is extended to all the elect under the New Covenant, as demonstrated by the conversion of Cornelius and his household in Acts.

Finally, the lesson underscores the responsibility of the church to preach repentance alongside faith in Christ. Citing Mark 6, the speaker affirms that the proclamation of repentance is a central component of the apostolic mission and remains a vital duty for every minister of the gospel. The session concludes by setting the stage for a future discussion on the practical application of true repentance in daily life.
